title: Map the Contributions before Combining Them
status: New proposed Lesson 08 production script, 2026-10-30. No new animation or narration in this handoff.
learningOutcome: Map proposals, reasons, limits and open questions without changing their ownership or support status.

scenario.kind: Original fictional discussion-training case with explicitly named snapshots
scenario.sourcePrompt: A community book club wants a 30-minute taster activity for new readers. Help them try discussing a short text and find out how the weekly club works. Your group should recommend one coherent activity and explain how it serves both aims. Use the main room, the supplied one-page text and club information sheet, and existing paper and pens; do not buy anything. Leave at least five minutes within the session for visitors' questions.

facts.text: The task is one coherent 30-minute taster activity, serving both trying a short-text discussion and learning how the weekly club works.
The main room, one supplied one-page text, a club information sheet, paper and pens are available. No purchases are allowed. At least five minutes for questions is included within the thirty minutes.
Maya proposes: Pairs could compare one line from the short text before we share anything with the whole group.
Noah proposes: A short demonstration could show newcomers what it means to give an interpretation and a reason.
The participant proposes: I suggest keeping time for questions about the club, using the information sheet for anything it actually answers.
Maya states partial support: I support showing an example, but I don't want it to take away the pair discussion.
Noah states partial support: I support some pair discussion. I still want us to decide how short the demonstration should be.
The participant states: I support protecting the question time. We still need a workable sequence within thirty minutes.
No complete sequence, stage durations or demonstration leader has been agreed. No taster has happened and no visitor result has been measured.

unknowns: The exact stage durations and whether an eventual detailed schedule fits
Who is willing and able to give the example
Which visitor questions the supplied information sheet will answer
Visitors' number, needs, preferences and willingness to share
Whether the group will adopt a complete proposal
How the activity would work in practice

baseline.meaning: All three proposals and the three explicit support statements are available as attributed source cards. The whole proposal remains open. Branch replies never become baseline facts.

proposal_check.proposal: We could begin with a brief example, use the same text in pairs, share one idea, and keep at least five minutes for club questions. Can we check the timing and who would give the example before we decide?
proposal_check.mayaReply: I support that sequence if the demonstration stays brief and the pair task remains.
proposal_check.noahReply: I support starting with an example and keeping question time. I am not ready to agree on the full sequence until we check the timings.
proposal_check.meaning: A labelled later authored check adds exactly these replies. Maya supports the sequence conditionally; Noah supports two elements and withholds support for the whole sequence pending timing. This does not establish a final group decision.

rehearsal.meaning: Use the explicit S05 proposal and replies as a frozen reference board, not as new speech to the learner. A private summary remains blank; the optional model is separate.

boundaries: Partial support attaches to a named element or condition; do not promote it to unconditional whole-group agreement.
No majority rule, unanimous decision procedure, assigned leader or final authority is supplied.
Thirty minutes is the activity duration, not a learner speaking limit or discussion deadline. The five-minute minimum is included, not added after thirty minutes.
At most twenty-five minutes remain for all other stages and transitions together, and fewer if question time exceeds five. This is a bound, not an agreed schedule.
A proposed demonstration leader is an unresolved dependency; do not assign Maya, Noah or an invisible facilitator without an authored decision.
The information sheet exists, but its complete contents are not supplied. Mark an unanswered question for checking; do not invent its answer.
Branch continuations and later model replies are authored examples, not observed real learner behaviour.
A coherent candidate can still need timing, accessibility and participation checks. Do not guarantee that a courteous summary wins agreement.

blocks.title: Keep the Shape of What Was Said
Separate a Limit from a Preference
Use the Map to Start a Check

L08.S01.c001.speaker: coach
L08.S01.c001.text: Several useful contributions do not yet make a shared proposal. First find out what each person has offered and what remains unsettled. A good summary makes the discussion easier to inspect. It does not turn the person summarising into the owner of everyone else's ideas.
L08.S01.c001.visualEn: Open on three attributed cards moving into a four-part board: proposal, reason, constraint, open question. No permanent character stage.
L08.S01.c001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.c001.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S01.c002.speaker: coach
L08.S01.c002.text: Our practice group is planning a thirty-minute book-club taster. It should let newcomers try discussing a short text and learn how the weekly club works. The main room and the stated materials are available. At least five minutes for questions belongs inside the thirty minutes.
L08.S01.c002.visualEn: Show the exact prompt in an accessible source panel; stage a two-aim board and a 30-minute bar with at-least-five marked inside, not after it.
L08.S01.c002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.c002.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S01.c003.speaker: coach
L08.S01.c003.text: Now look at three proposals already on the table. Keep each person's words available while you make shorter notes. A label such as pairs is useful for navigation, but it should not replace the important detail about discussing one line before whole-group sharing.
L08.S01.c003.visualEn: Show source cards for Maya, Noah and Participant beside compact notes; every card stays visibly attributed. These are prior proposals, not three new adopted stages.
L08.S01.c003.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.c003.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S01.d001.speaker: maya
L08.S01.d001.text: Pairs could compare one line from the short text before we share anything with the whole group.
L08.S01.d001.visualEn: Brief Maya bubble over her own source card, then return the same card to the board.
L08.S01.d001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.d001.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L08.S01.c004.speaker: coach
L08.S01.c004.text: That is a proposal about participation and sequence. We can ask why starting in pairs might help, but we should not silently add a reason that Maya has not given. Keep an offered action distinct from your own interpretation of its possible benefit.
L08.S01.c004.visualEn: Separate Maya proposed from Possible reason to discuss. The inferred-reason card has a question mark and explicit provisional wording, not a Maya quote.
L08.S01.c004.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.c004.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S01.d002.speaker: noah
L08.S01.d002.text: A short demonstration could show newcomers what it means to give an interpretation and a reason.
L08.S01.d002.visualEn: Brief Noah example; no agreement gesture from the other characters.
L08.S01.d002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.d002.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L08.S01.c005.speaker: coach
L08.S01.c005.text: Noah offers a short example and says what it would show. That purpose may connect with the pair task: newcomers could see the kind of contribution they will then try. It is a possible connection, not evidence that every newcomer will understand or feel ready.
L08.S01.c005.visualEn: Move the example card towards the pairs card with a dotted proposed link; preserve both names and no success checkmark.
L08.S01.c005.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.c005.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S01.d003.speaker: learner
L08.S01.d003.text: I suggest keeping time for questions about the club, using the information sheet for anything it actually answers.
L08.S01.d003.visualEn: Participant proposes questions with the information-sheet limit visible. No invented club schedule or membership policy appears.
L08.S01.d003.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.d003.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L08.S01.c006.speaker: coach
L08.S01.c006.text: Question time is not merely a third person's favourite idea. The prompt requires at least five minutes for it. By contrast, the order and length of the example, pair discussion and sharing are still proposals. Put these on different rows so a suggestion does not quietly override a requirement.
L08.S01.c006.visualEn: Move the five-minute minimum to the fixed-constraint rail while candidate stages remain on a proposed sequence rail.
L08.S01.c006.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.c006.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S01.c007.speaker: coach
L08.S01.c007.text: The available information sheet can support answers about the club. Its full contents are not supplied here, so we cannot promise it answers every visitor's question. A useful note can preserve that limit: answer what the sheet covers, and identify anything that still needs checking.
L08.S01.c007.visualEn: Show sheet as an existing resource with unknown coverage; a separate unanswered-question card stays open.
L08.S01.c007.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.c007.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S01.c008.speaker: coach
L08.S01.c008.text: It is tempting to tidy the board by removing repetition or uncertainty. Remove duplicate wording if it helps, but keep different conditions and unresolved questions. Two people can favour the same element for different reasons, and those reasons may matter when you decide how to use it.
L08.S01.c008.visualEn: Two support cards point to the same example card while their distinct qualifiers remain readable. Do not merge their source labels.
L08.S01.c008.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.c008.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S01.c009.speaker: coach
L08.S01.c009.text: Before combining anything, check your map against what was actually said. Have you kept the main proposal, the reason that was supplied, the fixed limits and the unresolved question? You do not need four boxes in every real conversation; you need enough structure to avoid losing a material distinction.
L08.S01.c009.visualEn: Reduce the full map to a compact inspection card; four categories are optional aids, not a compulsory speech formula.
L08.S01.c009.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.c009.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S01.c010.speaker: coach
L08.S01.c010.text: The next step is not to announce that everyone agrees. It is to ask which parts already have explicit support and which still need discussion. A clear map gives the group something concrete to correct before you invest in a combined plan.
L08.S01.c010.visualEn: End with the map becoming an editable draft summary, labelled Ready to check, not Agreed plan.
L08.S01.c010.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S01.c010.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S01.h101.purpose: Privately identify which contribution concerns the activity sequence and which protects a task requirement.
L08.S01.h101.visualEn: Keep the three attributed source cards. Leave the private answer area blank.

L08.S01.h102.purpose: Privately choose one open question that must remain visible before a whole proposal can be reported.
L08.S01.h102.visualEn: Show a blank question space alongside timing, example-leader and support placeholders; no suggested learner answer is inserted.

boundary: Use formal explanation and short explicitly fictional excerpts. Partial support, open questions, candidate proposals and adopted decisions stay distinct. A summary does not create consent. Models are separate authored examples, not captured learner speech.
